themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Deterioration Surge
themes_detail.summary: Street signs and street sweeping complaints spiked dramatically this week in CD 302, with street sweeping up 991% (15 complaints this week vs. 1.4 weekly average over 8 weeks) and damaged/dangling street signs up 471% (15 total sign complaints this week vs. 2.7 weekly average), suggesting a potential infrastructure maintenance breakdown or recent weather/construction event.
evidence: Street Sweeping: 15 complaints this week vs. 1.4 weekly average (991% spike, z-score: 9.12)
Street Sign - Damaged: 10 complaints this week vs. 1.8 weekly average (471% spike, z-score: 5.28)
Street Sign - Dangling: 5 complaints this week vs. 0.9 weekly average (471% spike, z-score: 4.45)
reporting_angles: Contact DOT and Sanitation to determine if recent weather, construction, or staffing changes triggered the spike
Walk affected streets in Fort Greene and Brooklyn Heights to document sign damage and sweeping neglect; interview residents about safety concerns

themes_detail.label: Graffiti and Illegal Posting Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints surged 193% this week (11 complaints vs. 3.8 weekly average, z-score: 5.21) and illegal posting complaints jumped 1500% three weeks ago (4 complaints vs. 0.2 weekly average, z-score: 8.66), indicating either a coordinated tagging campaign or sudden breakdown in enforcement across CD 302.
evidence: Graffiti complaints: 11 this week vs. 3.8 weekly average (193% spike, z-score: 5.21)
Illegal Posting: 4 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average (1500% spike, z-score: 8.66)
Combined visual disorder complaints trending upward over past 3 weeks
reporting_angles: Map graffiti hotspots in Fort Greene and Brooklyn Heights; interview residents and business owners about frequency and locations
Contact NYPD and Sanitation about whether this reflects organized tagging crews or reduced enforcement response times

themes_detail.label: Sewer System Distress
themes_detail.summary: Sewer complaints in CD 302 jumped 385% two weeks ago (20 complaints vs. 4.1 weekly average, z-score: 5.95), the highest spike among infrastructure issues, potentially indicating a developing system failure, blockage, or overflow event affecting multiple blocks.
evidence: Sewer complaints: 20 two weeks ago vs. 4.1 weekly average (385% spike, z-score: 5.95)
Spike occurred 2 weeks ago, suggesting potential ongoing issue
High statistical severity (z-score 5.95) indicates anomalous event
reporting_angles: Contact DEP to determine whether a sewer main break, blockage, or backup occurred 2 weeks ago; obtain emergency repair records
Interview residents in areas with concentrated sewer complaints about odors, backups, or overflow; check for public health notices

themes_detail.label: Food Safety Compliance Spike
themes_detail.summary: Food establishment complaints jumped 129% three weeks ago (18 complaints vs. 7.9 weekly average, z-score: 4.28) in CD 302, suggesting either a Health Department inspection sweep or emerging food safety violations at multiple venues.
evidence: Food Establishment complaints: 18 three weeks ago vs. 7.9 weekly average (129% spike, z-score: 4.28)
Spike occurred 3 weeks ago, showing some lag time in complaints
Represents sustained elevated concern about food safety
reporting_angles: Obtain Health Department inspection records for CD 302 from past month; identify which establishments had violations and what type
Interview restaurant owners and public health officials about whether a specific compliance issue (e.g., cold storage, pest control) triggered the spike

themes_detail.label: Drug Activity Sharp Rise
themes_detail.summary: Drug activity complaints spiked 500% this week in CD 302 (3 complaints vs. 0.5 weekly average, z-score: 5.0), a sharp jump that may signal either increased open-air drug use or heightened community reporting, especially relevant given recent subway safety incidents in Brooklyn Heights.
evidence: Drug Activity complaints: 3 this week vs. 0.5 weekly average (500% spike, z-score: 5.0)
Related context: Brooklyn Eagle reported woman arrested for subway slashing in Brooklyn Heights (March 22, 2026)
Convergence of emerging safety concerns in the district
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD and community leaders about whether this week's spike reflects actual increase in drug use or improved 311 reporting following recent subway crime
Investigate locations of complaints; cross-reference with subway stations and transit hubs in Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights to assess transit safety implications
